evidence.title: Why ASEAN’s coming digital economy trade agreement deserves your attention
evidence.body: [e001:f01] The former U.S. ambassador to Singapore on why ASEAN's landmark digital economy deal could create the world's next great growth story. [e001:f02] At a time when much of the world is building digital walls, Southeast Asia is trying something more ambitious: building a digital bridge. [e001:f03] Earlier this year, the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) concluded negotiations on the Digital Economy Framework Agreement, or DEFA—the world’s first comprehensive, region-wide agreement dedicated to the digital economy. [e001:f04] The pact is expected to be signed at the ASEAN Summit this November, when leaders from the group’s 11 member states will converge in Manila. [e001:f05] DEFA may sound like the sort of acronym-laden agreement that disappears quickly from the headlines. [e001:f06] The agreement is an attempt to do for the key elements of modern digital trade—data, digital payments, e-commerce, online consumer protection, and AI—what trade agreements once did for ports, tariffs and containers: create common rules and standards to drive seamless commerce across borders. [e001:f07] DEFA is an overlooked attempt to solve one of the digital economy’s defining problems: commerce is increasingly borderless, but the rules governing it are not. [e001:f08] Signing the agreement will only be the first step; ASEAN’s 11 members will have much work to do to make DEFA work in practice. [e001:f09] A benchmark study by Google, Temasek and Bain estimated that the region’s digital economy surpassed $300 billion in gross merchandise value in 2025. [e001:f10] ASEAN’s own studies project that the region’s digital economy could reach $1 trillion by 2030 on its current trajectory—and potentially touch $2 trillion if policymakers implement DEFA rules expeditiously. [e001:f11] But it will also bring about a deeper change that won’t show up in GDP figures. [e001:f12] Through rules that promote cross-border data flows, regional commerce, and harmonized cybersecurity standards, DEFA will help ASEAN embrace the modern-day digital economy. [e001:f13] At the same time, it is sending a broader signal to policymakers and corporate leaders around the world: integration still matters, even in this age of tariffs, trade wars, and digital sovereignty. [e001:f14] Global leaders should pay attention to DEFA, as it shows one way that regions can foster growth in the digital age without eroding trust, deepening inequality or stifling innovation. [e001:f15] The hard work comes after the ink dries in Manila, and it will require policymakers, industry partners, and civil society to bring the agreement to life. [e001:f16] Assuming the agreement can deliver these outcomes, DEFA will be remembered as more than a diplomatic milestone.

evidence.title: Thailand is taking the lead in discussions to boost investment between ASEAN and Hong Kong
evidence.body: [e002:f01] Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister announced the completion of negotiations for the ASEAN–Hong Kong Investment Agreement, enhancing market access and opportunities for investment in key industries and promoting stronger business ties. [e002:f02] Key Points Deputy Prime Minister and Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun announced the conclusion of negotiations for expanded investment market access under the ASEAN–Hong Kong, China Investment Agreement (AHKIA), with the First Protocol signed on September 20 in Manila. [e002:f03] The protocol aims to enhance market-access commitments, increasing investment opportunities, particularly in industries like automobiles, while fostering stronger supply-chain connections between Hong Kong investors and Thai companies. [e002:f04] Thai businesses will gain wider opportunities to invest in Hong Kong, potentially accessing the Chinese market via the Belt and Road Initiative, while maintaining compliance with domestic laws and government regulatory authority. [e002:f05] Thailand coordinated the negotiations, leading to the signing of the agreement’s First Protocol during the 10th ASEAN Economic Ministers–Hong Kong, China Consultation in Manila on September 20. [e002:f06] The protocol adds market-access commitments intended to create more investment opportunities and provide clearer conditions for businesses. [e002:f07] Thailand expects greater investment in industries such as automobiles, automotive components, and printed circuit boards, while developing closer supply-chain connections between Hong Kong investors and Thai companies. [e002:f08] Thai businesses will also gain broader opportunities to invest in Hong Kong, with potential access to the Chinese market through the Belt and Road Initiative. [e002:f09] Thailand’s commitments are consistent with existing domestic laws and preserve the government’s authority to regulate and determine public policy. [e002:f10] AHKIA originally covered investment protection, promotion, and facilitation, while negotiations on market access began in 2021. [e002:f11] Following legal review and verification completed in March 2026, the protocol expands the framework to provide greater transparency and predictability for investors while supporting technology, advanced industries, and regional supply chains. [e002:f12] Source : Thailand Leads Talks to Expand ASEAN-Hong Kong Investment。

evidence.title: Fed Rate Hike in October: What Investors Check Now
evidence.body: [e002:f01] The flash US purchasing managers' index has jumped to 58.4 points, its highest level since July 2021, and input prices are rising at a pace last seen in October 2022. [e002:f02] The futures market now prices a further Fed rate hike on October 28 at almost 70 percent, and the crypto market is falling broadly. [e002:f03] The most important date for the crypto market in the coming weeks is October 28. [e002:f04] That is when the US Federal Reserve decides on the policy rate again, and since September 23 the futures markets have held a further increase to be more likely than a pause. [e002:f05] For you as an investor in Germany, what counts is less the figure itself than the chain it sets off. [e002:f06] This piece places the data in context and then works through what there is to check in concrete terms: leveraged positions, the one-year deadline under Section 23 EStG, the buying route and custody. [e002:f07] US PMI Jumps to 58.4: What the Purchasing Managers' Index Actually Measures The purchasing managers' index, or PMI, is a monthly survey of company purchasing managers that puts every answer on a scale around 50 points: readings above 50 mean growth against the previous month, readings below it contraction. [e002:f08] Supplier delays were as widespread as at any time since July 2022. [e002:f09] That sub-index came in at 66.4 points in September, and the rate of input price inflation derived from it reached its highest level since October 2022. [e002:f10] Fed Funds Rate at 3.75 to 4.00 Percent: What Was Decided on September 16 The starting point for the current expectation lies a week back. [e002:f11] On September 16, 2026, the Fed's Open Market Committee raised the target range for the overnight rate by a quarter point to 3.75 to 4.00 percent, the first increase since July 2023. [e002:f12] Since September the question has been how much further it will raise. [e002:f13] A Rate Hike on October 28: What the Futures Market Prices In Under CME FedWatch The CME FedWatch tool is not a bank's forecast but a derivation: it works back from the prices of futures contracts on the US overnight rate traded on the CME to establish which rate decision the market is pricing in for each meeting date. [e002:f14] Following the PMI release, the daily market report of the KuCoin exchange dated September 24 gives a probability of 69.7 percent for an increase of 25 basis points in October. [e002:f15] For you in Germany the access route is what matters here: the US spot ETFs cannot be traded here, and the exchange route runs through debt securities on crypto, that is ETNs and ETPs. [e002:f16] If the yield on short-dated government bonds rises, so does the return an investor receives without price risk.

evidence.title: ‘The people are fed up’: Md. governor signs executive order targeting data centers
evidence.body: [e003:f01] Wes Moore signed an executive order targeting data centers in the state, though he stopped short of anything that resembled a moratorium. [e003:f02] Instead, he’s establishing new standards and calling on state lawmakers to repeal a law passed in 2020, which gave data centers certain tax exemptions. [e003:f03] The action makes it clear that before any new data centers can move forward with the required state-issued permits, the projects will have to be aligned with five new principles aimed at increasing accountability and transparency, which he touched on in a speech early this morning before signing the new order. [e003:f04] “Truthfully, the people are fed up, and so am I,” Moore said. [e003:f05] The order creates a single standard and review process for any large data center proposal in Maryland, which covers the permit and incentive process, as well as any public letter of support being sought. [e003:f06] It calls on data centers to hire local builders and make sure any new facility won’t add strain to the electric grid. [e003:f07] “Local governments know their communities better than anybody.” The governor is also creating a new task force with the power to review every project. [e003:f08] It will also maintain an online dashboard that lays out the plans and expected impact of any proposed data center. [e003:f09] The new rules come just days after Moore told Punchbowl News he would sign a data center moratorium if state lawmakers passed one, though the executive order stops short of proposing anything like that. [e003:f10] Don’t let him gaslight you.” Moore’s campaign countered by pointing out the bill the governor is pushing to repeal, exempting data centers from the sales and use tax, was sponsored by Cox when it passed in 2020. [e003:f11] Cox “rolled out the red carpet for data centers to come to Maryland,” said Carter Elliott IV, a spokesman for Moore’s gubernatorial campaign. [e003:f12] Data centers, which are helping to fuel the current AI boom around the country, are quickly becoming local political issues across the country. [e003:f13] Liberal and conservative leaders in Maryland have approved moratoriums at the local level. [e003:f14] Abigail Spanberger also issued an executive order aimed at further regulating data centers in the Commonwealth. evidence.title: いまさら聞けない「米国の雇用が世界経済にとって最も重要」なワケ…崩れたら株が「大暴落」（クーリエ・ジャポン）
evidence.body: [e005:f01] 【見る】プロこうして「上がる株」を判断する 分析に「本当に役立つ」指標の名前 【第3回】プロはこうして「上がる株」を判断する 分析に「本当に役立つ」指標の名前 なぜ投資には米国の指標が重要なのか ──著書の『武器になる経済指標』の冒頭は、米国の指標からはじまっていますが、なぜ米国から解説がはじまるのでしょうか。 [e005:f02] 米国は非常に大きな経済規模を持ち、1ヵ国で世界のGDPのおよそ4分の1を占めています。 [e005:f03] 世界中の投資家が米国の雇用統計を注視している理由としてポイントを挙げると、米国のGDPの約7割を個人消費が占めているからです。 [e005:f04] つまり、世界のGDPの約4分の1を占める米国経済の約7割が個人消費によるもので、これを単純に掛け合わせれば、米国の個人消費だけで世界経済の約2割を占める計算になります。 [e005:f05] では、米国の個人消費はどのような状況で伸びるのかと言えば、雇用が増加し失業率が安定しているときです。 [e005:f06] したがって、米国の雇用統計を確認されおけば、世界経済がどの方向に向かっているのかを、かなりの範囲まで把握できるのです。 [e005:f07] 日本では「令和のブラックマンデー」などと呼ばれましたが、その直前には、米国の雇用情勢が悪化しているのではないかという懸念が広がっていました。 [e005:f08] 当時は米国の失業率が上昇しはじめるなど、雇用市場の弱さを示す兆候が出ていたため、市場参加者が一斉にリスクを回避し、資金を引き上げる事態になりました。 [e005:f09] しかし、雇用統計も決して完璧なデータではありません。 [e005:f10] 米国ほど人口規模の大きな国で、毎月の雇用者数が10万人増えたのか、15万人増えたのかという違いは、誤差の範囲です。 [e005:f11] 雇用統計の速報値には一定のノイズが含まれていて、2ヵ月ほどかけて修正された結果、実際にはそこまで「雇用が弱い」という現象はありませんでした。 [e005:f12] 最近では、むしろ雇用者数の勢いが戻りつつあるので、現時点では、最も重要な米国の雇用と個人消費が大きく崩れる事態には至っていません。 [e005:f13] 米国の雇用統計が堅調である間は、中長期的に見れば、世界経済や世界の企業収益全体が改善していく可能性が高く、それに伴って株価も上昇していくと考えられます。 [e005:f14] 米国の雇用が減少方向に向かいそうだから、株をすべて売却するべきかと言えば、そう単純な話でもありません。 [e005:f15] しかも単なる景気を下支えするだけでなく、その後は需要を強く刺激する方向に政策が動いたため、結果として株価が大きく上昇する展開にもなりました。 [e005:f16] 次ページは：「AIバブル」が「ITバブル」と異なる理由 前へ 1 2 次へ 1 / 2ページ 【関連記事】 2030年、日本円は「70円台」の超円高に…日本人だけが気づかない「為替」の意外な盲点 「絶対にやめろ」の忠告を無視…1日で2400万円を失った投資家の末路 給料が上がっても喜べない…日本を破壊する「賃金上昇」の意外な落とし穴 プロはこうして「上がる株」を判断している…企業分析に「本当に役立つ」指標の名前【エコノミストが明かす】 日本株「爆上がり」のウラで、賢い人が「避けている」投資先の名前。

evidence.title: Nasdaq hits record high as U.S.-Iran talks rattle oil prices
evidence.body: [e002:f01] The Nasdaq gained 0.5% on Tuesday, reaching an all-time intraday peak and finishing the session at a record close. [e002:f02] The Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 0.4%, while the S&P 500 ended fractionally in the red, still sitting roughly 0.7% short of its all-time high. [e002:f03] Heading into Wednesday's session, U.S. equity futures were little changed. [e002:f04] S&P 500 futures pointed modestly upward, Nasdaq -100 futures slipped 0.1%, and Dow futures trailed by 25 points, equivalent to a 0.1% decline. [e002:f05] November Brent futures were changing hands near $99.60 a barrel, a gain of roughly 0.4%, whereas West Texas Intermediate futures retreated 0.6% to $89.97 a barrel. [e002:f06] President Donald Trump disclosed Tuesday that American and Iranian representatives convened for three hours alongside the United Nations General Assembly in New York. [e002:f07] He called it a "very good meeting." Earlier that day, in his address to the UN, Trump said he faced a "big decision" over whether to pursue a deal with Tehran or "annihilate" the country. [e002:f08] The dollar advanced to a near two-month peak on a trade-weighted basis, according to The Wall Street Journal , propelled by the Federal Reserve's increasingly hawkish posture on inflation working its way through global currency markets. [e002:f09] The euro, yen, and pound all fell against the greenback. [e002:f10] European gasoil futures surged more than 4% after Trump signaled support for a ban on U.S. diesel exports. [e002:f11] The national average price for diesel reached $6.53 per gallon, according to AAA. [e002:f12] Wednesday morning brought declines across European equities, with the Stoxx 600 retreating as Brent crude climbed again. [e002:f13] Across the Asia-Pacific region, South Korea's Kospi added 0.9% and Australia's S&P/ASX 200 posted a modest gain, while mainland China's CSI 300 dropped 0.6%. [e002:f14] Traders on Wednesday will be watching earnings results from General Mills $GIS , Paychex, and H.B. [e002:f15] The Treasury Department is also set to reveal the size of its next bond-buyback operation, according to The Wall Street Journal.
